name: shell-plugins-selective-least-privilege-00b8
instr:
Give callers least-privilege control over credential provisioning across environment, command-line, file, and cache outputs. Callers can preview applicable work without revealing credentials, then understand the outcome of every operation. Existing unrestricted provisioning remains compatible while remote and direct use behave identically.

A policy selects indivisible operations by stable identifier or output channel, with denied work producing neither output nor operation-specific preparatory side effects and an absent policy allowing existing behavior. Planning is deterministic, secret-free, ordered by each adapter's declarations, and describes operation channels, groups, prerequisites, and context-dependent applicability. Execution gives exactly one secret-free produced, denied, skipped, unavailable, or failed decision per planned operation while preserving established prerequisite diagnostics. Across AWS, CrateDB, GitHub, ngrok, PyPI, Redis, and Vercel, grouping preserves aliases and paired arguments while independent values remain independently selectable. Permitted operations retain existing overrides, missing-field handling, host classification, constructor behavior, and command placement without reordering caller arguments. File and cache prerequisites are authorized separately from credential exposure, so denial prevents related reads, provider retrieval, probes, and mutations. RPC carries the same policy and preserves stable identifiers, plans, decisions, outputs,
